label: Bible Study
prompt: And I will make of thee a great _____, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
verse: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
note: God's call to Abram — one childless old man, promised a great nation and a great name.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Draw _____ to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
verse: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
note: Draw nigh, and He draws nigh — the shortest distance in the Bible is one step toward God.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a _____ to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
verse: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
note: A camel through a needle's eye — Jesus' deliberately absurd picture, and the disciples were exceedingly amazed.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Beat your _____ into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong.
verse: Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong.
note: Joel flips Isaiah and Micah's famous peace line into a call to arms for the valley of decision.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, _____, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
verse: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
note: 'Stedfast, unmoveable' — two KJV spellings in a row that spellcheck would flag. Paul's charge after the resurrection chapter.
